source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 6: Show that the determinant equals (x+4)(x-2)^2 (book page 60).

blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant factorises as \((x+4)(x-2)^2\).
Every row adds up to \(x + 4\), so adding the columns gives that factor.
Plan: \(C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\), take \(x+4\) out, make zeros, read the triangular form.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} x & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = (x+4)(x-2)^2\)
Method: Property vii (add columns; subtract rows), Property v (factor out), Property viii (triangular determinant).

Add all columns into column 1
\[C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} x+4 & 2 & 2 \\ x+4 & x & 2 \\ x+4 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Each row: \(x + 2 + 2 = x + 4\).

Take \(x+4\) out of column 1
\[\Delta = (x+4)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & x & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property v.

Subtract row 1 from rows 2 and 3
\[R_2 - R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = (x+4)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & x-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & x-2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(x - 2\), \(2 - 2 = 0\). Now the determinant is upper triangular.

Multiply the diagonal
\[\Delta = (x+4) \cdot 1 \cdot (x-2)(x-2)\]
\[= (x+4)(x-2)^2\]
Why: Property viii.

Check with a number
\[x = 0:\ \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 0 - 2(-4) + 2(4) = 16\]
\[(0+4)(0-2)^2 = 16 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Expansion along row 1 gives the same value as the formula.
